newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed off on Wednesday with many investors staying sidelined.
Dealers foresaw little business in the near future if Germany and France did not agree to the EMU stability pact.
They said the market was short of financial data today, but they expected some action if tomorrow's U.S. retail sales or Friday's U.S. PPI data proved to be disappointing.

Dealers were split on possible swap opportunities between Dutch and German debt. "Dutch bonds are likely to perform better as Germany is still creating uncertainty about its reserves to meet EMU-standards," said one dealer.

Another dealer said the current yield gap looked promising for German debt. "Germany is likely to outperform the Dutch market in the near future with a yield gap close to minus 15 basis points for the 10-year Dutch bond compared to the equivalent German bond," he said.
Bond prices were edging up around midday, following German bund futures contracts. The June future contracts rose to 101.05, but this did not hold.
"The June contracts could fall to 99.50 in near future," said one dealer, adding the market was still bearish.
